<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d62cfdd4f607579163fa5dc59817007c2dbf8b1b` — the merge of head `82fb363acae6bdb5cfb6dbaef380036f54e2647c` into base `f47f7f222f1c8c03ab866efa428f4b50ff72b9b8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

## Contract review

Check-runs read at 2026-10-22T22:07Z: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(5/6)` and `(6/6)` are `success`; `Test Core (2/6)` and `(4/6)` were still `in_progress` at that read and are reported as pending, not as passes. The dogfood battery does not run on a PR head (two speeds), so the dogfood evidence is the dev's cited run, judged in ③.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the code at the head.

1. **New exports, additive.** `QueryPageWindowSchema` (`z.number().int().nonnegative()`), `QueryPageWindowParamSchema` (that number, or a non-blank string whose `Number(text)` is one, transformed to the count) and the four ADR-0122 aliases (`QueryPageWindow`, `QueryPageWindowParsed`, `QueryPageWindowParam`, `QueryPageWindowParamParsed`) land in `data-engine.zod.ts:927-957` and are recorded in `api-surface/data.json`, `export-origins/data.json`, `declaration-map/data.json`, `json-schema.manifest/data.json`. **Right.** `check:spec-parsed-alias` demanded the `Parsed` alias and the dev added it; every artifact gate is green on the head.

2. **`QueryWithTransportSchema` canonical `limit` / `offset` / `top`: any number → non-negative safe integer** (`describedPageWindowMember`, `data-engine.zod.ts:1347-1348`, applied in the `extend` at `:1376-1378`). A door parses this: `POST /data/:object/query` validates `FindDataRequestSchema` before `findData` (`crud-routes.ts:353-367`) and the runtime dispatcher's POST twin does the same (`domains/data.ts:242-243`). **Right — a narrowing of a published request schema a door enforces.**

3. **`QueryTransportParamsSchema` `$top` / `$skip` / `skip` number arm: `z.number()` → `QueryPageWindowSchema`** (`:1023`, `:1026`, `:1059`); the string arm stays `z.string()` at the member and is judged by the fold (`lowerFoldedTransportValues`, `:1187-1194`) through `QueryPageWindowParamSchema`, refused at the canonical path naming the spelling, one diagnostic — the shape `query-transport.test.ts` already pinned. **Right.** Residue, accepted as the dev declared it: `QueryTransportParamsSchema` parsed on its own still admits any string on those three keys. No door parses the fragment alone (`FindDataRequestSchema.query` reaches it only through `QueryWithTransportSchema`; the only other mentions in `packages/spec/src` are comments in `odata.zod.ts` and the `FindDataRequestSchema` docblock), and the JSON Schema string arm could not carry the rule either way (ledgered, item 9).

4. **`HttpFindQueryParamsSchema.top` / `.skip`: `z.coerce.number()` → `QueryPageWindowParamSchema`** (`protocol.zod.ts:2378-2379`). Declaration-only on the wire: `GET /data/:object` hands `req.query` whole to `findData` (`crud-routes.ts:160-165`), the dispatcher's GET rides it verbatim (`domains/data.ts:410`), and no package parses this schema at run time (the client cites it as the declaration, `client/src/index.ts:371`). The TypeScript input type narrows too, from `unknown` (coerce) to `number | string`. **Right — GET's runtime answer is byte-unchanged, the published declaration now matches it.**

5. **The normalizer reads the spec's bound.** `pageWindowValue` (`protocol.ts:4787-4789`) replaces the restated predicate (`Number.isSafeInteger` and non-negative, over a trimmed `Number(text)`) with `QueryPageWindowParamSchema.safeParse(value)`; refusal code `INVALID_REQUEST` and text unchanged. `metadata-protocol` already imports from `@objectstack/spec/data` (`protocol.ts:175-181`), so no layering inversion. **Right — same accept set, one declaration, both sides read it.**

6. **Declared accept set equals the normalizer's, per parameter.** Integer: zod 4 `.int()` is the safe-integer check on both sides. Minimum: 0 on both (`0` stays a window; `$top=0` asks for the total alone). Maximum: `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` on both; the JSON Schema number arm publishes `integer`, `minimum 0`, `maximum 9007199254740991`. String coercion: on both sides a non-blank trimmed string converted by `Number`, so `' 5 '`, `'1e2'`, `'0x10'` are counts on both and blank / whitespace / `'abc'` / `'-1'` / `'1.5'` are refused on both. `?page=`: a window on neither side — `page` sits in `QUERY_PARAM_NEAR_MISS` (`protocol.ts:4573`), a hint table whose header says nothing in it is accepted as input; `?page=2` is refused as an unknown parameter with a "did you mean the 'skip' query parameter" tail, so no schema should declare it and `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` rightly does not. **Right.** The equality is pinned where the brief asks: `protocol.page-window-declared.test.ts` uses the real `findData` with a recording engine as the oracle (accepted iff the engine is reached, with the window it received), 13 schema rows × 17 numbers + 18 strings + 3 others, a non-vacuity check first, number-only members asserted to refuse every string as before.

7. **Scope measure — every schema left alone is out by evidence, not assertion.** `EngineQueryOptionsSchema`: its one reader outside the spec is `action-execution.ts:1997`, `Object.keys(shape)` (a key set, no parse). `QuerySchema` (`query.zod.ts:555-557`): the driver contract and the recursive `expand` value, neither judged by the normalizer; its three members are overridden on `QueryWithTransportSchema`, so the door's declaration narrows without touching it. `get_record.limit` (`builtin-node-config.zod.ts:628`): the executor hands it to `data.find` / `data.findOne` (`crud-nodes.ts:530-548`), the `IDataEngine`, never `findData`. `ListRecordResponseSchema.pagination` (`contract.zod.ts:441-448`): a response. `AuditMetaItemRequest` / `HistoryMetaItemRequest` / `ListNotificationsRequest` `limit` (`protocol.zod.ts:1823`, `:1921`, `:3284`): metadata and notification routes whose own text says the server clamps, never refuses — not the data list doors. `DataEngineFindRequestSchema`: no reader outside the spec. `ODataQuerySchema.$top` / `$skip` (`odata.zod.ts:186`, `:197`, already `.int().min(0)`): its docblock records that it grades no runtime door. The MCP `query` tool (`mcp-http-tools.ts:866-867`) already declares `int().positive().max(...)` / `int().nonnegative()` and is not a published spec schema. `findData` callers (`crud-routes.ts:165`, `:375`; `data-action-routes.ts`; `action-execution.ts:675`; `connector-pull.ts:343`; `import-runner.ts`) are the two REST doors plus server-built or schema-less in-process windows. **The dev's table is right in every row.**

8. **One door answer moves, in its code only.** On `POST /data/:object/query` and the dispatcher twin, a malformed window is now refused by the body schema: `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `fields[0].field` = `query.limit` / `query.offset` (`crud-routes.ts:361-366`; `requestSchemaRefusal`, `domains/data.ts:114-128`), where it was `400 INVALID_REQUEST` from the normalizer. Still 400, still before any read (`data-page-window-door.test.ts` pins zero driver reads on both doors). GET unchanged. **Right as implemented; the rule reading is in ③.**

9. **Dropped-refinements ledger.** Two new sites — `data/QueryPageWindowParam` `options[1].in` and `api/HttpFindQueryParams` `top.options[1].in` — and the header counts move 240 → 242, 811 → 813. The string arm's rule is `Number` semantics, which `PROJECTABLE_REFINEMENT_PATTERNS` has no arm for and no pattern writes without approximating; `build-schemas.ts` holds the ledger equal to the generator and is green on the head. **Right.**

10. **Generated references** (`content/docs/references/**`) regenerated, `index.mdx` counts 1542 → 1544. `check:docs` green. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — true.** Nothing widens an accept set or a public surface; two published request schemas narrow, which `clause2-line.mjs` names as the arm's defining case (not a widening, but breaking). The `fix(spec)!:` title carries the same fact.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — true.** The kind is the change to what a metadata author can write. No authorable metadata schema embeds `QueryWithTransportSchema`, `QueryTransportParamsSchema`, `FindDataRequestSchema` or `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` (`packages/spec/src` at the head: `protocol.zod.ts`, the catalog string in `plugin-rest-api.zod.ts:1020`, and comments). `QuerySchema` is untouched. The card named the authored flow `query` window; the dev measured, and I confirm, that `get_record.limit` never reaches the normalizer (item 7), so it is not narrowed here, no `authorable-surface/` baseline moves, and no flow migration row is owed by this PR.
- **`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — true under the rule of record.** `pr-automation.yml` WHICH LEVEL and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: the level follows the metadata protocol alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its carriers. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (launch-window guard plus level axis) is green in `Check Changeset`. The `metadata-protocol` entry is a behaviour-preserving refactor (item 5).
- **Carriers present.** The `**BREAKING**` banner, the before / now / remedy prose, and both declaration lines are in the changeset body; the PR body carries the same two lines.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — right.** No metadata type, authorable key, object definition or stored row is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the remedy line prescribes a request value, not a metadata rewrite; the vocabulary is ADR-0087's addendum and `check-adr-0087-registration` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question (dev recommends A) — A, decided by the rules.** The card's acceptance line reads "no door's runtime answer changes (the server already refuses these)". Declaring the window on `FindDataRequestSchema` moves four POST body shapes (`limit` / `offset` negative or fractional) from the normalizer's `400 INVALID_REQUEST` to the body schema's `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[0].field` naming `query.limit` / `query.offset`; status, timing (before any read) and GET are unchanged, and the REST pin was updated to say so. Rules: Prime Directive #10's corollary (never advertise what the runtime does not deliver; declared ≠ enforced is fixed, trimmed or filed, and the claim is kept as narrow as the enforcement, judged at every call site) and Prime Directive #12 (one strict internal contract, refused at the boundary) decide for A, with ADR-0049 as the recorded principle that a spec declaration must match what the runtime enforces. The card's own Wanted line asks that each schema a judged door reads declare the bound, and `FindDataRequestSchema` is the one schema a door actually parses (`crud-routes.ts:359`, `domains/data.ts:242`) — B keeps on it exactly the gap the card was filed for. ADR-0112 does not prefer one 400 catalog code over another here; it asks that a failing request answer a catalog code in the standard envelope, and `VALIDATION_FAILED` + `fields[]` is the envelope this door already answers for every other malformed member, `{"limit":"ten"}` included, so A removes a dialect rather than adding one. Recorded plainly for the seat: the acceptance line's literal "answer" reading is not met for the code and envelope of those four POST shapes; its parenthetical (the refusal already exists) is the invariant that holds. No escalation needed.

**`(narrowing)` dogfood — met on the head's runtime, by the measured delta.** The os-dev rule names the final head. The dev's run: tree `3fead31f3`, packages built at `685efa48a`, VERDICT exit 0, 289 files passed and 3 skipped, 2491 tests passed and 18 skipped. Measured at the head: `685efa48a..82fb363a` touches four files — one `export type QueryPageWindowParsed` line (erased at run time), the ledger header counts in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, and one regenerated line each in `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json`; `3fead31f3..82fb363a` is those two JSON lines alone. Neither ledger has a runtime reader in `packages/qa/dogfood/**` or `packages/spec/src/**` (every mention is a comment). The built packages and the tree the suite ran against are runtime-identical to the head, and the reading is cited with its tree as AGENTS.md asks. Accepted; any further commit on the PR makes a new head that owes its own run.

**Out-of-scope findings (os-dev-report 6351947108):**
1. *`get_record.limit` is `z.number()`; its executor hands it to ObjectQL `find` / `findOne`, never `findData`.* **Card.** It is a metadata-authoring trap under Prime Directive #10's filing test: the schema (`builtin-node-config.zod.ts:628`) admits a fraction or a negative, and both executor branches (`crud-nodes.ts:530-548`) need a positive integer — `limit` above 1 reaches the driver's LIMIT as written, so `2.5` meets the driver; anything else selects `findOne`. Rightly not in this PR: it is authored flow metadata, so its fix is `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor`, with a migration line — the opposite declaration from this PR's. Evidence for the card: the contract text above and that repro; no producer in `examples/**` or HotCRM `4166f2146bec`, so low priority. Who acts: `domain:spec` with `domain:automation`.
2. *`HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` declares only `top` / `skip` while GET also takes `limit` / `offset` / `$top` / `$skip`; declaring them is a widening.* **No card.** Not a defect, a contract violation or a trap: nothing the schema declares is false, every declared parameter is served, the extra spellings are published on the POST transport declaration, and `GET /data/:object` is excluded by name from the closed-set rule as an OPEN parameter set, so a "complete" GET declaration would not be a closed set either. It belongs in the PR's acceptance notes, where it is. If a consumer ever needs the GET declaration to carry every spelling, that is its own `Clause-②: yes (widening)` card with that consumer as evidence.
3. *Windows inside a nested `expand` query are judged by no one.* **No card from this PR's evidence.** `QuerySchema.expand` values are nested QueryAST whose own description states that per-parent `limit` / `offset` / `orderBy` are NOT applied on the expand path, so the claim is already as narrow as the enforcement and there is no server bound to declare. If anything it is a liveness question about a declared key that is applied nowhere, for the `Spec property liveness` ledger's owner, not a window-bound narrowing for this lane.

**Other flags.** None of the three needs the maintainer. The PR touches no governed surface, is 467 changed lines, and its head repo is the base repo. Pending at review time: `Test Core (2/6)` and `(4/6)`; the queue requires their green independently of this record.
